5.0.0.en: Now gather thyself in troops, O daughter of troops!

5.0.1.en: He hath laid siege against us:

5.0.2.en: they shall smite the judge of Israel with a rod upon the cheek. [1]

5.0.3.en: The call is addressed to the enemies of Zion, who had armies desiring victory over Israel and Judah, so that all her cities are besieged by divine permission to chasten His people.

5.0.4.en: The prophet Micah turns to what will befall Israel, when Assyria takes her captive, while Judah withstands the repeated siege of Assyria, until she is taken captive in stages, ending through Babylon in the days of King Zedekiah, and her complete ruin is accomplished at the hand of Titus in AD 70.

5.0.5.en: The king, the nobles and the religious leaders were preoccupied with wealth and power, and thought they were safe within the fortified walls of Jerusalem, and they did not realize that she would be besieged and destroyed, and that her judge or her king (Zedekiah) would be unable to protect her. Zedekiah, the last king of the offspring of David, was sitting on the throne of Jerusalem when Nebuchadnezzar seized it (2 Kgs 25:1).

5.0.6.en: * Thus he says that Samaria will be surrounded and besieged by hostile peoples. Not only will they strike her cheek with their heads, which could be borne, but they will crush her with staves, which carries a special cruelty. This means the humiliating, wretched ordeal of captivity, for without dispute a blow on the cheek carries a special insult. Notice that they also strike her with staves, causing violent troubles along with insult. Samaria was humiliated, since the tribe of Ephraim ruled her. She was in shame and under sufferings. In any case the striking hands will cease, and we shall not taste misery if we do what we can to remove the wrath of the Lord from all because of disobedience and the eager commission of sins, which the Lord hates. If instead of this we honor Him with a virtuous life, then we enjoy prosperity and live a joyful life worthy of praise.

5.0.7.en: St. Cyril the Great. Some see that the prophet Micah addresses his words here to the army of the Roman Titus, who besieged Jerusalem, because she struck her Judge, the Lord of glory Jesus, on the cheek, and insulted Him, saying: "Prophesy, who is it that smote thee?"

5.1.s.en: 2. The birth of the eternal King:

5.1.0.en: 2 But thou, Beth-lehem Ephratah, though thou be little among the thousands of Judah, yet out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel; whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting. 3 Therefore will he give them up, until the time that she which travaileth hath brought forth: then the remnant of his brethren shall return unto the children of Israel.

5.1.1.en: But thou, Beth-lehem Ephratah, though thou be little among the thousands of Judah, yet out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel; whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting. [2]

5.1.2.en: When the king is unable to protect Jerusalem and cannot save her, a marvelous king arises in a small village thought to be of no account among the thousands of villages of Judah, an eternal King who enters human history, able to save completely. The first dies and passes away in disgrace and shame, and the second reigns forever in the heavens, and His kingdom shall not pass away.

5.1.3.en: The expression "whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting" is unique to the Lord Christ alone, as the One eternally begotten, the only-begotten Son of God. For this reason He says: "Before Abraham was, I am" (Jn 8:58). And the Psalmist says: "From everlasting to everlasting, thou art God" (Ps 90:2).

5.1.4.en: Perhaps some may ask: How does he say, "that is to be ruler in Israel," when Israel condemned Him to crucifixion, and He did not set Himself up as king over Israel? He said: "My kingdom is not of this world" (Jn 18:36). He reigned over the new Israel, the holy Church, as "the head over all things to the church" (Eph 1:22). He displayed His authority over nature, and over death and diseases; was He then unable to reign over Israel? They wanted to make Him king, and He passed through the midst of them and they did not see Him!

5.1.5.en: Though both Israel and Judah fall into captivity, true reform is accomplished at the hand of the One born in Beth-lehem Ephratah, our Lord Jesus Christ. He is born in this humble place, in a village of His forefather, the great David.

5.1.6.en: Some tried to attribute this prophecy to Zerubbabel, but St. John Chrysostom explains that it does not apply to him. For on the one hand the prophet did not say "he will dwell in Beth-lehem" but "out of thee shall he come forth," and on the other hand Zerubbabel's goings forth are not "from of old, from everlasting"; rather it applies to Jesus Christ, the eternal Word.

5.1.7.en: In the dialogue of Tertullian the scholar with the Jews, he relies on this prophecy that was fulfilled literally in the person of Jesus Christ, and that now no one from the tribe of Judah from Beth-lehem remains in whom the prophecy could be fulfilled in another.

5.1.8.en: * Peace to Beth-lehem, the house of bread, in which was born the Bread that came down from heaven (Jn 6:51).

5.1.9.en: Peace to Ephratah, the land of fruitfulness and fertility, whose fruit is the Lord Himself.

5.1.10.en: Micah prophesied of you of old: "And thou Bethlehem... art not the least among the princes of Juda..." (Mt 2:6). For in you was born the Ruler, the One born before Lucifer. He whose birth from the Father is before time, and the cradle of the race of David continued in you until the Virgin brought forth her Son, and the remnant of the people who believed in Christ returned to the children of Israel preaching to them freely with words like these: "It was necessary that the word of God should first have been spoken to you: but seeing ye put it from you, and judge yourselves unworthy of everlasting life, lo, we turn to the Gentiles" (Acts 13:46).

5.1.11.en: St. Jerome. * He showed the truth as it is written of Jesus Christ, "though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor"; for this reason He chose a poor mother from whom He was born, and a poor homeland.

5.1.12.en: Origen the scholar. * It is not the divinity that came from Beth-lehem but the humanity, yet He did not stop at this point, but rather went forth from there with His divinity, as in the words "whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting."

5.1.13.en: St. John Chrysostom. * By designating the location of Beth-lehem, (the Jews) were like those who built Noah's ark, providing others with the means of escape while they themselves perished in the flood. They were like signposts that show the way but are unable to walk in it. They were asked: Where should Christ be born? They answered: "In Bethlehem of Judaea: for thus it is written by the prophet" (Mt 2:5). They repeated from memory what had been written about this by Micah: "And thou Bethlehem, in the land of Juda, art not the least among the princes of Juda: for out of thee shall come a Governor, that shall rule my people Israel" (Mt 2:6).

5.1.14.en: St. Augustine. * He who is before the ages, who was with God from the beginning, who is God the Word, whose origin is from the beginning, received birth according to the flesh in you (O Beth-lehem), and made you famous and radiant, though you are of no importance among the thousands of Judah.

5.1.15.en: * The blessed Apostle reminds us of the blessing of Judah, pointing out how it reached its fulfillment: "For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda" (Heb 7:14). So also the prophet and the Evangelist Matthew. The former spoke prophesying, and the latter linked the prophecy to his story. What is strange in this, when he says that the evident enemies of the truth told Herod plainly that Christ would be born in Beth-lehem, since it is written: "And thou Bethlehem, in the land of Juda, art not the least among the princes of Juda: for out of thee shall come a Governor, that shall rule my people Israel" (Mt 2:5-6). Let us add what the Jews omitted because of their malice, making the testimony incomplete (for they did not mention to Herod the rest of the prophecy). For the prophet, after saying "out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel," added "whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting" (Mic 5:2).

5.1.16.en: * By saying "out of thee shall come a Governor" he makes clear the economy of the Incarnation, and by adding "whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting" he proclaims His divinity, and that He is begotten of the Father before the ages.

5.2.0.en: Theodoret, Bishop of Cyrus. Therefore will he give them up, until the time that she which travaileth hath brought forth: then the remnant of his brethren shall return unto the children of Israel. [3]

5.2.1.en: The Lord gave them up to distress so that they might look for His coming, born of the Virgin, as the prophet Isaiah, a contemporary of the prophet Micah, prophesied of Him; and the latter specified the town of His birth.

5.2.2.en: With the coming of the King the Savior, the believing remnant returns to establish the Church of the New Testament, the new Israel. This holy remnant, which receives the Messiah the Savior, walks in the spirit of the fathers, the holy men of God. And so "the heart of the children to their fathers" is turned (Mal 4:6).

5.2.3.en: Some see that the "remnant" here refers not only to the believers from among the Jews but also from among the Gentiles, as all are joined to the fold of "the new children of Israel," as the Apostle Paul says: "And came and preached peace to you which were afar off, and to them that were nigh. For through him we both have access by one Spirit unto the Father. Now therefore ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God" (Eph 2:17-19).

5.2.4.en: And as the Jews are gathered together with the Gentiles in one faith, they become brethren to one another, "for which cause he is not ashamed to call them brethren" (Heb 2:11).

5.2.5.en: * He distinguishes between "them which were afar off, and them that were nigh" (Eph 2:17). This points to the Gentiles and the Jews. For the Jews are quite clearly nigh and the Gentiles afar off. Yet the Savior Himself brought the Gospel to the Gentiles. Paul indicates here first that Christ by His coming truly preached peace to those afar off, that is, to the Gentiles, as appears from many testimonies. For those who came to the faith from a Gentile origin had a greater claim to be called sons than those of Jewish origin. But it cannot be denied that the others received it too, and for this reason he added "and to them that were nigh."

5.3.0.en: And he shall stand and feed in the strength of the LORD, in the majesty of the name of the LORD his God; and they shall abide:

5.3.1.en: for now shall he be great unto the ends of the earth. [4]

5.3.2.en: He carries out the shepherding Himself in the name of God the Father, for the two have one administration, so the name of the Lord Jesus is glorified and reaches the ends of the earth.

5.3.3.en: The prophet sees in this King a good shepherd who feeds his people in the strength of the Lord, and it was said of the Lord Christ: "He taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes" (Mt 7:9).

5.3.4.en: * The authority of His teaching was so great that it seized many of them and drove them to great amazement. Because of their delight in what He said, Jesus asked them not to depart until the end of His discourse. For not only did the hearers not leave Him after He came down from the mountain, but the whole multitude followed Him because of the greatness of the love He showed in His discourse. Most were amazed because of His authority. For when He spoke of those matters He did not point to another, as the prophet Moses did, but everywhere He showed that He is the One who has authority to give the decision. And when He laid down the laws Jesus added: "But I say unto you" (Mt 5:22, 28, 32, 34, 39, 44). And when He reminded them of the day of the last judgment He showed that it is He who will carry out justice, whether by punishments or by honors. This is what caused agitation among them.

5.3.5.en: St. John Chrysostom. Before His ascension Jesus came and spoke to His disciples, saying: "All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth" (Mt 28:18).

5.3.6.en: If the kings of the two kingdoms, Israel and Judah, and their princes and armies, could not protect them, the divine Shepherd guarantees the peace of His kingdom, and keeps His people, not from Assyria or Babylon, but from the devil and all the powers of darkness.

5.3.7.en: He is the marvelous Shepherd who raises up shepherds and gives them Himself to work in them and through them, until perfect peace is accomplished through His holy sacrifice.

5.4.0.en: 5 And this man shall be the peace, when the Assyrian shall come into our land: and when he shall tread in our palaces, then shall we raise against him seven shepherds, and eight principal men. 6 And they shall waste the land of Assyria with the sword, and the land of Nimrod in the entrances thereof: thus shall he deliver us from the Assyrian, when he cometh into our land, and when he treadeth within our borders.

5.4.1.en: And this man shall be the peace.

5.4.2.en: When the Assyrian shall come into our land: and when he shall tread in our palaces, then shall we raise against him seven shepherds, and eight principal men. [5]

5.4.3.en: (Verses 5-6) are a poetic piece of ten lines depicting the Assyrian invasion, against which a number of national princes are raised, seven shepherds and eight princes, so that the invader turns back to his country in failure. These princes unite together so that one ruler appears who delivers from Assyria.

5.4.4.en: The Lord Christ is called "our peace" (Eph 2:14), as He accomplishes peace between man and the Father, and also grants peace to the soul with the body, and peace among men, as among the nations. St. Hippolytus sees that Assyria here points to the Antichrist.

5.4.5.en: Assyria was the most dangerous enemy at that time, and here it points to the devil, the enemy of good, the opponent of the Church of Christ; but the enemy of good will surely be defeated, and the victory will be for the Church of Christ.

5.4.6.en: Who are the seven shepherds and the eight princes whom the new King raises up from among men? The number 7 points to perfection in this world, and the number 8 points to entering beyond time and passing into eternity. The servants of Christ ought to be perfect shepherds in the Lord, and heavenly kings not drawn away by the glory and riches of the world. Their law is "divine peace," for the Lord Himself is their peace. The Lord Christ said: "Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid" (Jn 14:27).

5.4.7.en: The enemy of good does not cease to storm our inner land by every means, in order to seize it for himself, so that it becomes a kingdom of darkness instead of a kingdom of light. He wishes to tread in our palaces, and so defile our hearts, which are the temple of God, with the Spirit of God dwelling in them. The war is between God and the devil, and the battlefield is our inner depths; if we accept His shepherding we shall surely enjoy His victory.

5.4.8.en: The prophet Isaiah depicted for us the work of this King the Shepherd and His shepherding through His servants, saying: "Behold, a king shall reign in righteousness, and princes shall rule in judgment. And a man shall be as an hiding place from the wind" (Isa 32:1-2). It is as though this heavenly King who became man has opened His side for us that we may hide in it when the winds and storms of the devil rage against us! He is our impregnable fortress, and a refuge for us in the midst of trials.

5.4.9.en: Theodoret, Bishop of Cyrus, sees in his commentary on Isaiah (Isa 32:1) that this text does not apply to Hezekiah or Josiah or Zerubbabel. [A person must understand the king to be Christ our Lord, and the princes to be the holy Apostles and those who succeeded them, as they were appointed to direct the churches. The blessed David proclaimed of them: "Instead of thy fathers shall be thy children, whom thou mayest make princes in all the earth" (Ps 45:16)].

5.4.10.en: * It seems to me that he points to the Apostles, who became teachers in her (in the Church). And in describing their authority, power and glory he says: "whom thou mayest make princes in all the earth" (Ps 45:16)... Remember that the Apostles went about the whole world, and became princes more sovereign than all the other rulers, and with more authority than the emperors. The emperors have their authority while they are alive, but when they die they have it no more; the Apostles have authority while they are alive, and it increased all the more at their death. And while the laws of the emperors have their force within the borders of their countries, the commands of the fishermen extend to every place in the world. The Roman emperor cannot issue laws for the Persians, nor the Persians for the Romans, while these Palestinians legislated for the Persians and the Romans and the people of Thrace and the Scythians and the Indians and the Moors and the whole world. Their laws remained in force not only while they were alive but also after their death, and those who submitted to them preferred to lose their lives rather than turn back from these laws.

5.5.0.en: St. John Chrysostom. And they shall waste the land of Assyria with the sword, and the land of Nimrod in the entrances thereof: thus shall he deliver us from the Assyrian, when he cometh into our land, and when he treadeth within our borders. [6]

5.5.1.en: "The land of Nimrod" is another name for Assyria, and here it symbolizes all the evil nations.

5.5.2.en: Father Victorinus, Bishop of Petau, sees that Nimrod points to the Antichrist, and that the Lord Christ sends seven shepherds, who are the seven great archangels, to strike the kingdom of the Antichrist.

5.5.3.en: If the enemy has entered our land and trodden our borders, then through the direct shepherding of the Lord Christ, and His shepherding through His Apostles, the battle turns in our favor, and the kingdom of the devil collapses as by a sword, and we escape from his hand, repeating the words of the Savior: "Be of good cheer; I have overcome the world."

5.6.s.en: 5. An ecumenical extension of the shepherding:

5.6.0.en: And the remnant of Jacob shall be in the midst of many people as a dew from the LORD, as the showers upon the grass, that tarrieth not for man, nor waiteth for the sons of men. [7]

5.6.1.en: After speaking of the Good Shepherd who chose His disciples and Apostles to work through them, and how the battle turned into victory for us and the collapse of the kingdom of the devil, the prophet presents to us a wonderful picture of the Church and her work on an ecumenical level.

5.6.2.en: She is "the remnant of Jacob," the very few who received faith in the Lord Christ, and enjoyed the descent of His Holy Spirit upon them on the day of Pentecost to be the leaven that leavens the whole lump. She goes forth "in the midst of many people," working by the Spirit of the Lord for the salvation of many from all nations and tongues and peoples. She is scattered throughout the world to be its salt and its light. By this the spiritual kingdom of Christ is established.

5.6.3.en: They are "as a dew from the LORD"; they do not work with a fanatical human mind, but with a heavenly mind that descends like dew from the Lord. They have been born from above, and so they offer heavenly things so that all may share with them the sweetness of the new heavenly life.

5.6.4.en: They are "as the showers (the rains) upon the grass, that tarrieth not for man, nor waiteth for the sons of men," that is, they do not rely on human support but on the free grace of God. They water others with the waters of the Spirit, like heavenly rain from the Lord, in which no man has any merit.

5.6.5.en: When he speaks to us of the new flock under the care of the divine Shepherd, he announces the spiritual victory full of sweetness, so that the Church in the world becomes like dew from the Lord and like the summer shower in beauty, gentleness, refreshment and radiance.

5.6.6.en: The remnant of Jacob is the spiritual Israel, or the company of true believers; they are like the divine dew, a secret of blessing and growth for many. These blessings do not come from men but are "from the LORD."

5.7.0.en: 8 And the remnant of Jacob shall be among the Gentiles in the midst of many people as a lion among the beasts of the forest, as a young lion among the flocks of sheep: who, if he go through, both treadeth down, and teareth in pieces, and none can deliver. 9 Thine hand shall be lifted up upon thine adversaries, and all thine enemies shall be cut off. 10 And it shall come to pass in that day, saith the LORD, that I will cut off thy horses out of the midst of thee, and I will destroy thy chariots: 11 And I will cut off the cities of thy land, and throw down all thy strong holds: 12 And I will cut off witchcrafts out of thine hand; and thou shalt have no more soothsayers: 13 Thy graven images also will I cut off, and thy standing images out of the midst of thee; and thou shalt no more worship the work of thine hands. 14 And I will pluck up thy groves out of the midst of thee: so will I destroy thy cities. 15 And I will execute vengeance in anger and fury upon the heathen, such as they have not heard.

5.7.1.en: And the remnant of Jacob shall be among the Gentiles in the midst of many people as a lion among the beasts of the forest, as a young lion among the flocks of sheep: who, if he go through, both treadeth down, and teareth in pieces, and none can deliver. [8]

5.7.2.en: In the preceding passage he depicted the Church in her gentleness toward the peoples because she offers living fellowship with God, yet she is strong in the Spirit, shattering and scattering the strongholds of darkness.

5.7.3.en: The prophet likened the believers at one time to dew, which softens and refreshes plants in an atmosphere of calm, and likened them also to the rains that water the fields, and now to lions among the beasts of the wilderness, whom all fear.

5.7.4.en: The believer is marked by pure love flowing from the depths as a gift of the Holy Spirit to him, and by firmness against evil, corruption and error. For this reason the Apostle Paul calls his disciple Timothy to strive as a good soldier of Jesus Christ, and the Lord Christ points to the strength of believers in the truth, saying: "which all your adversaries shall not be able to gainsay nor resist" (Lk 21:15). And the Apostle Paul speaks of the believers' resistance to the devil and his hosts: "the weapons of our warfare... mighty through God to the pulling down of strong holds" (2 Cor 10:4-5).

5.8.0.en: Thine hand shall be lifted up upon thine adversaries, and all thine enemies shall be cut off! [9]

5.8.1.en: Victory is accomplished for the new Israel, so that she is like a lion, like a mighty warrior shattering her spiritual enemies. This battle is completed when God puts all enemies under the feet of Christ the Head of the Church (1 Cor 15:25-28).

5.8.2.en: The Psalmist sees the hosts of demons collapsing before the Church of God, and sings, saying: "the people fall under thee" (Ps 45:5).

5.8.3.en: And it shall come to pass in that day, saith the LORD,

5.9.0.en: that I will cut off thy horses out of the midst of thee, and I will destroy thy chariots: [10]

5.9.1.en: When the Lord dwells in the heart and reigns, we do not need military power, but the great power of God. We repeat with all our strength: "Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me" (Ps 23:4).

5.9.2.en: The secret of the Church's strength is the almighty Lord, not the human arm and human ability, so the Lord cuts off the horses from her midst and destroys her chariots, that she may enjoy the Spirit of the Lord, who lifts her from glory to glory, and she walks in the world like one ascending in a chariot of fire.

5.9.3.en: The Church, the new Israel, enjoys many divine blessings: 1. The removal of the material instruments of war, horses and chariots [10], so that the Church relies not on material things but on the surpassing grace of God. "And I will cut off the chariot from Ephraim, and the horse from Jerusalem" (Zech 9:10). 2. He cuts off from her the cities of the earth to give her heavenly cities, and throws down her temporal strongholds so that He Himself may be a wall of fire for her [11]. 3. The removal of vain worship with all its accompaniments of witchcraft and soothsaying [12]. 4. The removal of every idol in the heart, so that the Lord may set up His throne in it and occupy it completely [13]. 5. The enemy of good and his hosts fall under the divine wrath [15].

5.10.0.en: And I will cut off the cities of thy land, and throw down all thy strong holds: [11]

5.10.1.en: The Lord removes from His Church her earth, making her a second heaven in which He dwells. And He throws down all her temporal strongholds so that He Himself may be a wall of fire around her. It is as though their cities are turned from military cities into cities for dwelling, and the Lord guards them, for He is "their rock and their fortress and their deliverer" (Ps 18:2).

5.10.2.en: And I will cut off witchcrafts out of thine hand; and thou shalt have no more soothsayers:

5.11.0.en: Thy graven images also will I cut off, and thy standing images out of the midst of thee; [12]

5.11.1.en: The Lord removes from her all witchcraft and soothsaying (divination, or the claim to foretell future matters by the power of Satan), and opens her eyes by His Holy Spirit so that she recognizes the divine mysteries instead of the satanic works!

5.12.0.en: and thou shalt no more worship the work of thine hands. [13]

5.13.0.en: And I will pluck up thy groves out of the midst of thee: so will I destroy thy cities. [14]

5.13.1.en: The Lord removes the groves, that is, the wooden pillars set up as a symbol of Ashtoreth, the goddess of the Canaanites.

5.14.0.en: And I will execute vengeance in anger and fury upon the heathen, such as they have not heard. [15]

5.14.1.en: He concludes his discourse with a warning to whoever refuses to believe in the Savior, the Shepherd of souls, for he falls under the wrath and does not enjoy the heavenly blessings.

5.14.2.en: Who is there to shepherd me but You!

5.14.3.en: * Who else would shepherd my soul but You!

5.14.4.en: There is none who loves me and gives Himself for me but You!

5.14.5.en: The shepherding of men without You is destruction to my soul!

5.14.6.en: Your shepherding is unique and marvelous!

5.14.7.en: * You came to me in Beth-lehem, and made it the house of the heavenly Bread!

5.14.8.en: He who eats of You shall never hunger, and he who drinks of Your love shall never thirst!

5.14.9.en: You came to us, O Ancient of Days, O Eternal One, to carry me with You into Your eternity!

5.14.10.en: * You were born of a virgin, O Creator of the world!

5.14.11.en: And You have made of me, the servant, a little brother, and have given me sonship to Your almighty Father!

5.14.12.en: * You chose for Yourself disciples and Apostles, and made them princes and shepherds who bear the spirit of Your shepherding!

5.14.13.en: I see You transfigured in them, and I enjoy Your marvelous work through them!

5.14.14.en: You gave them authority over the powers of darkness.

5.14.15.en: By You they crushed the devil under their feet!

5.14.16.en: * You gave them Your Holy Spirit to shepherd Your people.

5.14.17.en: So they drew souls from all nations and tongues and peoples.

5.14.18.en: They became dew to the world, offering every fatherly kindness!

5.14.19.en: They became like the rain that turns wildernesses into a heavenly garden.

5.14.20.en: * They accepted to be lambs among wolves, devoured by the wolves, who then become gentle lambs!

5.14.21.en: You gave them the spirit of power to face error, so they became lions that are not afraid!

5.14.22.en: * By Your shepherding You gave Your people Your surpassing peace!

5.14.23.en: You cut off their horses from their midst and destroyed their chariots, for You became for them a heavenly wall of fire that keeps them!

5.14.24.en: You cut off all witchcraft and soothsaying, for You revealed to them the mysteries of Your heavens!

5.14.25.en: What a marvelous divine Shepherd You are!
